subtitle: Lesson 109 · Transactions, Locking, and Isolation Levels

code:
-- A statement's row/page locks on one table or index
-- cross roughly 5,000 locks held at once
-- -> SQL Server escalates them into ONE table lock
caption: Automatic, built-in — no setting requests it.
A statement can start well-behaved and change behavior partway through.

code:
-- Before escalation: other sessions on unrelated rows -- FINE
-- After escalation:  same sessions -- suddenly BLOCKED
-- (the table lock covers rows the UPDATE never even touched)
caption: "Why did the whole app just freeze for 30 seconds?"

code:
-- No setting turns escalation off.
-- Break one huge batch into smaller batches,
-- each comfortably under the lock-count threshold.
caption: Smaller batches never accumulate enough locks to trigger it.
